Title: Case 000: The Till Roll
Briefing: Mechanics test, not canon. Sarah Mercer finished a late shift at the Bluebell Diner on Thursday 12 October 2000 and was never seen again. The original inquiry settled on her leaving alone at about eleven. The box has come back up from the archive. Read the file, speak to who you can, and tell me what you can actually establish.

Questions.Text: When did Sarah leave the diner?

Facts.Text: She left with someone, in a car

Questions.Text: Who was the last person known to have seen Sarah?
When did Mick Hollis leave the diner?
Whose was the dark estate car outside after half eleven?

Characters.Name: Lorraine Pike
Characters.DefaultLine: I don't know, love. It's a long time ago.
Characters.RefusalLine: I've said all I'm going to say.

Responses.Line: Sarah left about eleven. Said goodnight and walked off to the bus stop on her own. I cashed up and locked the door behind her.
I know what I saw. I've told it the same way for twenty-six years. Don't put words in my mouth.
I've been turning it over. She went out the front about eleven, I do know that. But she used to have a cigarette out there. She might have come back in. I couldn't swear to it now.
Good worker. Never late. Kept herself to herself that last month, mind. I thought it was money.
Mick Hollis. In every night, same table by the window. Harmless. He'd nurse one pot of tea for two hours.
Now I think about it, he was still at his table when I started cashing up. I'm nearly sure. I remember going round him with the mop.
He rang me. First time in years. Wanted to know what I'd been saying to you. I didn't like it.
Me? I was there eleven years. I'd have noticed if something was wrong. That's what I can't forgive myself for.
I never saw a car. I was out the back with the bins and the float.
Half eleven? But she'd gone. I... I was sure. It's twenty-odd years, love. I'd have sworn it.
I've looked at it. I don't know what to tell you. Those are her initials.
You're telling me I've had it wrong all this time? In front of her mother, at the inquest? No. No, I won't have that.
That's my signature. That's what I said, and it's what happened.
Half ten? Well. If that's what he says.
Doreen Ash was never away from that window. If she says there was a car, there was a car. Doesn't mean it was waiting for Sarah.
I wouldn't know one car from another, love.

Characters.Name: Mick Hollis
Characters.RefusalLine: Mick Hollis will not speak to you without a solicitor, and he has not appointed one.

Responses.Line: Same as I told them at the time. Had my tea, left about half ten. Sarah was still serving when I went.
I've said. I stayed a bit later than I told them. She locked up and walked home on her own. That's all there is.
I gave her a lift. Dropped her at the end of her road, about midnight. She got out and I drove home. I never saw her again.
Nice lass. Always had time for you. Not like some of them.
I never laid a finger on her. Write that down.
She was on with Sarah that night. Ran the place, really. That's all I know about her.
What about me? I had my tea there. It's not a crime.
I had a car, yes. Most people did. What of it?
It was parked up the road. I walked to it after she'd gone. On my own.
It was my car. I've told you now. I gave her a lift.
Are you accusing me of something? Because if you are, I want a solicitor, and until then I've nothing to say. We're done.
What's that got to do with me? I'd gone by then.
She was working late. I've said that.
That's what I said then and it's what I'm saying now.
I was frightened, all right? A lass goes missing and you're the last one in the cafe. You'd have said the same.
There you are, then. She left on her own. Lorraine saw her.
Plenty of dark cars about. It's a main road.
Are you accusing me of something? Because if you are, I want a solicitor, and until then I've nothing to say. We're done.
I told you. She walked.
All right. All right. She got in the car. I gave her a lift, that's all it was. Dropped her at the end of her road about midnight. That's the last I saw of her, and that's the truth.
That was me. I've told you.
I had an Astra. So did half of Nottingham.
All right. I stayed for a bit. Not long. I didn't want to be the last one there, did I? But she walked home on her own.
It's a car. It proves I had a car.
You've been straight with me, so. She got in the car. I gave her a lift to the end of her road. About midnight. I've carried that for twenty-six years.
Yes. That's the car.

Evidence.Name: Till roll, Bluebell Diner, 12/10/2000
Evidence.Description: The day's till roll, seized the following week. Each sale is printed with the time and the server's two-letter code.

Media.Caption: Watch: the till roll on your desk
Media.Transcript: The till roll from the Bluebell Diner, out of its evidence bag for the first time in years. The paper has yellowed and the ink has faded, but the columns can still be read.

Findings.Text: The last sale of the night is keyed under server code "S.M." at 23:32.

Interpretations.Text: Someone else used Sarah's till code. It says nothing about when she left.

Evidence.Author: TillRoll.C.Lorraine
Evidence.Name: Witness statement of Lorraine Pike, 14/10/2000
Evidence.Description: Taken two days after Sarah was reported missing.

Media.Caption: Watch: the Bluebell Diner at closing (reconstruction)
Media.Transcript: Reconstruction, not evidence. The diner after closing on a wet October night: chairs up on the tables, the mop bucket out, the coffee machine still warm.

Findings.Text: "Sarah left about eleven. She said goodnight and walked off towards the bus stop on her own."

Evidence.Author: TillRoll.C.Mick
Evidence.Name: Witness statement of Michael Hollis, 15/10/2000
Evidence.Description: Taken as part of house-to-house and regulars enquiries.

Findings.Text: "I had my tea and left about half ten. Sarah was still serving when I went."

Media.Caption: Watch: the view from Doreen Ash's window (reconstruction)
Media.Transcript: Reconstruction, not evidence. The diner and the main road as they would have looked through the rain from the house opposite, late on a wet October night.

Findings.Text: "There was a dark estate car parked outside with its engine running. It was after half eleven because the news had finished."

Interpretations.Text: Someone was waiting for Sarah to finish.
A car on a main road. It tells us nothing.

Evidence.Name: DVLA keeper record, Michael Hollis, 2000
Evidence.Description: Vehicles registered to Michael Hollis in October 2000. Has to be requested.

Findings.Text: Registered keeper of a dark blue Vauxhall Astra estate. One of the commonest cars in Britain at the time.

Interpretations.Text: The car Doreen Ash saw was probably Mick's.
Thousands of people drove one. It proves nothing.
